ruling.recommended_action: Record the RD-1 breach on the driver's file (unexplained +3.64 km off-route segment on a fixed-quote RydeX trip); no monetary refund is due since the fare was a fixed quote and none of the billed components exceed the quote. Note the driver's route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 for future repeated-breach review.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the only substantive statements are the rider's complaint (route/detour grievance) and the driver's statement "The GPS rerouted me, that's all. Nothing wrong with the fare." [F8]. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere in the record [F7][F8], so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation. safety_concern = none.

Rule 1 — the deviation exists. GPS shows +4.5 km / +42% against the optimal route [F1], a single off-route segment 14:19–14:26 covering 5.03 km where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, adding 3.64 km and reaching 1160 m from the optimal route [F3]. This is well beyond map-matching noise, so RD-1 is engaged: the driver's duty was the shortest and most direct route absent reasonable cause.

Rule 2 — no segment is exempted. There was no in-app chat at all [F7], so there is no rider consent before the segment to bring RD-5 into play (no message, no named road, no general route authorisation). The driver's "the GPS rerouted me" is a post-trip statement [F8], not a rider consent, and a driver's account is a claim, not consent (RD-5 / G11). Nor is it a RD-3 rider-named stop: no rider message named any place. Traffic does not excuse it: the only traffic facts are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY and CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY [F9][F10] — band 4 is not band 1 or 2, and in any event a lone band reading cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b) (MVP does not exempt on it alone) and no incident was recorded near the route [F11]. Weather was fair [F12]. So the whole 3.64 km segment [F3] remains an unexempted deviation and the driver breached RD-1.

Rule 3 — money. This is a non-metered service (RydeX), so the fare was a fixed quote taken at booking (F6 breakdown: base $3.90 + distance $15.06 for 10.68 km + time $4.50 for 17.3 min + platform $1.47 = $24.93, no surge [F5], no waiting). RD-2's non-metered branch refunds only ERP/toll actually incurred on the unexempted segment and unpublished post-trip add-ons (FARE-1). Extra kilometres do not change a fixed quote: billed distance 10.7 km equals the optimal route 10.7 km [F4], so no mileage overcharge reached the rider. There is no toll/ERP fact in the table (no `tolls` field, so FARE-2 is not triggered), the waiting fee was $0.00, the platform fee $1.47 is a published fee, and no unpublished add-on was appended. Refundable amount = $0.00 → RD-2 directs no_action while recording the RD-1 violation.

Rule 4 — flag. RD-6 requires a refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 violation AND route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1. The driver profile shows 4 disputes in 90 d with 2 upheld, both route [F14], i.e. route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 ≥ 1, and an RD-1 breach is recorded here. RD-6 is therefore satisfied independently of the monetary outcome, so flag_account = true for account review. The rider's profile [F13] (0 upheld) plays no part, and per the procedural rule profiles never decide the case on their own.

Evidence status: sufficient — GPS, fare breakdown and traffic coverage settle every element needed; no gaps (there is simply no chat, which is a finding, not a missing record).

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 14:19–14:26 added 3.64 km, reaching 1160 m from the optimal route [F3]. There are no chat messages at all [F7], so no rider message before the segment agrees to it; the driver's post-trip 'the GPS rerouted me' statement [F8] is a claim, not rider consent (RD-5/G11). No rider-named stop (RD-3) and no qualifying traffic cause: band 4 on AYE/CX [F9][F10] is not band 1–2 and never exempts alone (RD-4(b)), and no incident was recorded [F11]. The segment is unexempted and counts as a deviation.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's statement that 'the GPS rerouted me' [F8] is an untimed post-trip narrative with no traffic incident backing it; the only traffic records show band 4 mid-range speeds on AYE/CX [F9][F10], which cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b), and no incident was recorded near the route [F11]. It does not explain away the 3.64 km deviation.

The rider's fare grievance yields no refund: RydeX is a fixed-quote service, billed distance equals the optimal route [F4], no surge applied [F5], and every component of the $24.93 charge [F6] is a published item; no ERP/toll or unpublished add-on exists to refund under RD-2/FARE-1.
